title: Massive Selloff Today: Start Of Something Bigger? | Ole Hansen
speaker: Ole Hansen (Saxo Bank), host David Lin

macro_themes.view: Rising funding costs and borrowed hyperscaler capex mean the market now demands AI returns; buy-every-dip mechanics have changed.
Crude flows have recovered but refined products and LNG lag far behind, keeping diesel and crack spreads very elevated.
Energy-driven inflation keeps 3-4 hikes priced by next summer, a headwind for gold short term.
France's 10y above 5% and ~170bp over Bunds; things may have to get worse before reforms happen.
Low storage and competition with Asia for LNG mean higher prices if the winter is cold.
A 14% speculative unwind plus harvest supply; El Nino keeps the space volatile.

calls.reason: The true delivered cost is ~$30 above screen price from ship-to-ship transfers; the risk of renewed disruption before the midterms can't be ruled out.
calls.quote: Brent crude at 112 is is not really the right price. We should probably add potentially another $30 on top.

calls.condition: any further disruption to flows could force prices even higher
calls.reason: Inventories near record seasonal lows, refinery maintenance ahead and winter heating demand: no relief seen into early 2027.
calls.quote: the next few months will be quite critical and and any further disruption to to flows could... force prices even higher.

calls.reason: Storage at multi-year lows and Qatar LNG at ~20% of pre-war volumes.
calls.quote: generally a very cold winter and we will be paying higher prices this winter.

calls.condition: hedge funds turn long only once gold regains 4230-4250 (September low)
calls.reason: Hedge funds/CTAs are selling while ETFs and China/India demand accumulate; rate-hike pricing and a firm dollar hurt short term.
calls.quote: I maintain my long-term bullish view for gold 10 20% higher in a year from now, but in the short-term clearly challenged

calls.reason: The uptrend is intact on scarcity and Chinese refiner cuts, but AI-related weakness and US stockpiles flowing back could slow it near term.
calls.quote: I stay in the bullish camp on copper, but also just like gold acknowledge the fact that there are some headwinds in the short term

calls.reason: Shallow bounces and rising funding costs signal risk-off; buy-the-dip sentiment has been knocked, though no key level is broken.
calls.quote: that we come from this worst period where basically any dip should be bought... That seems to that sentiment seems to have taken a a knock back

notes: Date spoken by host (October 22nd). Timestamps are mm:00 from the transcript's minute markers; interview is 40 min. Gold 10-20% upside is given as a percentage (~4400-4800 from ~4000), so target left null. ULSD price '$200 plus' is in cents/gal terms as quoted. The NQ short-term bearish view is weakly implied.
